title: A very subjective comparison of Claude Code, OpenCode, Cursor & GitHub Copilot
summary: Maximilian Schwarzmüller's subjective comparison of Claude Code, OpenCode, Cursor and Copilot: all decent, features converge.

assertions.quote: ultimately, all these tools are decent

verdicts.note: By 2026 the major tools all offer agents, CLIs, cloud runs and review; differences are workflow and pricing more than capability.

assertions.quote: especially that combination of Claude Code with those models is really good

verdicts.note: Models are tuned on their vendors' harnesses and often score higher there, but third-party harnesses sometimes match or beat them on benchmarks (e.g. Terminal-Bench).

assertions.quote: Cursor, for example, has, uh, amazing auto-completion

verdicts.note: Cursor's indexing and model choice are accurate; 'most integrated' is a taste judgment and competitors have closed gaps.

assertions.quote: Claude Code, Cursor, and I guess also GitHub Copilot in the end are all heavily subsidized

verdicts.note: Heavy users clearly consume more compute than flat fees cover, which is why vendors added weekly limits; whether plans are below cost on average is not public.

assertions.quote: every provider tries to have its own configuration

verdicts.note: AGENTS.md vs CLAUDE.md vs .cursor/rules and different skill folders are documented differences; standardization is ongoing.

assertions.quote: the most important part will always be your prompt, the context you provide

verdicts.note: As models improved, output depends more on relevant, high-signal context than phrasing; consistent with Anthropic/Cursor guidance and long-context degradation evidence.
